title: Installed Sensor Enrollment Request v1
description: Consumes a one-use Discovery bootstrap credential that is already bound server-side to the existing organization tenant UUID, source profile, scope and expiry. The installed product proves possession of its installation key and reports exact component provenance; it never chooses its producer ID, installation ID or producer epoch.

idempotency_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the required Idempotency-Key header. The installation proof signs this digest, and admission rejects a header/body mismatch. The raw key is never persisted.

organization_tenant_id.description: The existing Quilr organization/workspace tenant UUID carried by the Discovery bootstrap. Admission requires an exact match to the bootstrap's server-side tenant binding.

bootstrap_id.description: Public identifier for the one-use Discovery bootstrap credential presented in the Authorization header. The raw bootstrap secret MUST NOT appear in this body or be persisted.

client_nonce.description: At least 128 bits of client-generated entropy, encoded base64url without padding.

publicJwk.description: Public asymmetric installation key only. Admission base64url-decodes every coordinate, verifies the exact curve length and point/key validity with a vetted crypto provider, rejects private/unknown members, and never treats this JSON shape as proof by itself.

key_thumbprint.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint over exactly the required public JWK members in RFC 8785/JCS lexical order; admission recomputes it after cryptographic key validation.

request_digest.description: RFC 8785 JCS SHA-256 of the enrollment request with installation_proof.request_digest and installation_proof.detached_jws omitted.

detached_jws.description: RFC 7797 detached JWS over the RFC 8785 canonical request with installation_proof.detached_jws omitted and installation_proof.request_digest present. The protected header requires typ=starliner-installation-proof+jws, the declared alg, key thumbprint as kid, b64=false and crit=[b64]; admission verifies the asymmetric signature and recomputed request digest. Regex acceptance is never sufficient.
